newsitem.title: CHINA: Jinqiao's boosting net masks problems - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Jinqiao's boosting net masks problems - analysts.

text.p: Major real estate company Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development Co, reported a 75 percent jump in profits on Friday, but analysts said the result masked problems.

The firm's basic business is selling land in the Pudong development zone to the east of Shanghai's city centre, where the real estate business boomed at the beginning of 1990s but is now facing a downturn.

Jinqiao's 1996 post-tax profit was 102.165 million yuan in 1996, up from 58.275 million yuan in 1995 based on international accounting standards, said a company statement in Friday's Shanghai Securities News.
But under domestic accounting standards, the 1996 net profit was only slightly up at 113.466 million yuan against 106.473 million yuan in 1995, it said.
Analysts said they were puzzled by the surge in profits, given the fact that the company's land sales do not appear to have increased much in 1996 over 1995.
"I have not seen any great improvement in the company's sales of land," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage. "The surge may have been brought about by some accounting-related issues."
The company's annual report includes an item called "adjustment of former year's losses or benefits", amounting to 81.42 million yuan or 62.34 percent of its pre-tax profit of 130.59 million yuan.
A company spokesman declined to explain this item, or to give details of the source of the profits.
"The performance of a company which relies on land sales is going to be unstable," said an analyst with one of the biggest domestic brokerages.
"Many areas around Shanghai are providing more preferential land prices to attract investment, which is providing strong competition (for Jinqiao)," he said.
The company's report said turnover in 1996 rose to 593.186 million yuan from 516.364 million yuan in 1995 based on domestic accounting standards.

"Government support is very important to a company like Jinqiao," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage. "If the company cannot get preferential treatment from the government, its outlook will be not be so good."

General Motors Corp and state-owned Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp on Tuesday signed a $1.57 billion joint venture to produce cars in the Jinqiao area, but analysts said the deal would not boost the company's 1997 outlook.
"The deal may bring some profit to the company, but it is only one project and will not boost the company's 1997 results given the weak real estate market in Shanghai," said a local analyst.
The company spokesman also said the project would not generate much profit for the company.
"It is a key project supported by the government, so it is impossible to sell (them land) at a good price," he said.
Jinqiao's B share price ended at $0.560, down $0.020 or 3.4 percent on Friday compared with Thursday's close. Its A share price fell 1.13 yuan or 6.5 percent to 16.23 yuan.

Analysts attributed the fall in prices to its unsatisfactory dividend plan. Jinqiao offer of a pre-tax cash dividend of 0.1 yuan per share for all shareholders from its 1996 profit and a three-for-10 rights issue at 3.5 yuan to 4.0 yuan each in 1997, the company statement said.
Jinqiao's earnings per share is 0.233 yuan based on 1996 net, up from 0.218 yuan in 1995, the company statement said.
($1 = 8.3 Chinese yuan)
